title: Engine Builder
intro: The easy one, and the one people ruin by making it hard. Twenty-two minutes at a pace you could hold a conversation at.
This is the base that lets you recover between points and between sessions. Going harder does not make it work better, it just turns it into a different session that you already do elsewhere.

before.label: Not today
before.text: A knee, hip or ankle that hurts when you pedal? Get it looked at first.

before.label: Stop and get it checked
before.text: A sharp pain, pain that spreads, numbness, or a joint that gives way.

before.label: Stop now
before.text: Chest pain, dizziness, a heartbeat that races or skips, or breathing that doesn't feel right. Get it looked at before you train again. Told to be careful with hard exercise? Check with your doctor first.

exercises.name: Easy Spin

good: Upright bike, sit tall with your hips above your knees
Easy enough to breathe through your nose
bad: Using an air bike — it rounds your lower back and drives it with every stroke

exercises.note: An incline treadmill walk does the same job if you prefer.

good: Hold the fence, stand tall, let the leg swing freely
Build the range across the ten
bad: Arching the back to throw the leg higher

good: Drive the back hip down, then rotate and reach tall
Feel the front of the back hip open
bad: Rotating before the hip has opened

exercises.name: Steady Ride

good: One pace the whole way, no surges
You should be able to talk in full sentences
bad: Drifting faster as you get bored, or chasing a number on the screen

exercises.note: Conversation pace. If you cannot talk, you are going too hard.
